the Candida cytoplasmic protein cytochrome c has cancer-specific binding activity and is a target antigen for a cancer-associated human monoclonal antibody HB4C5.
a mouse MAb raised against Candida cytochrom c was found to react with a cancer-specific antigen in human cancer tissue.

a mouse monoclonal anti-Candida krusei antibody (HCC 6- 3) that does not react with Candida cytochromec on nitrocelluose membrane, but does react with Candida and human lung cancer cytochrome c by the ELISA method, was found to react with human lung cancer tissue specifically.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mouse monoclonal anti-Candida cytochrome antibodies, except for the three clones, are not reactive with bovine cytoplasmic proteins.

a mouse monoclonal anti-cytochrome c, HCC 6.3, which was not reactive with transblotted Candida cytochroine c but was inhibited in ELISA with added cytochrome, was reactive to the cancer cells of the cytoplasm specifically.

the monoclonal antibody from clone HCC 5, 6, and 17 reacted with Candida cytochromes c specifically, whereas that from clone HCC1 reacted to cytochromes of other origins, including Candida cytochrones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytochrome c of C. krusei, which is recognized by the cancer-associated human monoclonal antibody HB4C5, is recognized by the mouse monoclonal anti-cytochrome c antibody HCC 6–3.
this antibody of clone HCCC 6-3 is cancer-specific and binds to a cytoplasmic antigen in human lung cancer cells.

the Candida cytoplasmic protein cytochrome c was recognized specifically by the mouse monoclonal anti-cytochrome c antibody, HCC 6.3, which was not cross-reactive with the bovine cytochromes c and which was reactive with human cancer tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a monoclonal antibody of mouse origin can recognize an antigen of cancer cells specifically, and this antibody is directed to a cytochrome c of Candida kruse.

the Candida cytoplasmic protein, cytochrome c is recognized as an antigen by a mouse monoclonal and a human monoclonal antibodies and that the Candida antigen is specifically recognized by the human antibody HB4C5 which is known as a cancer-associated antigen.
a monoclonal antibody, which does not react with a cytochrome c antigen in a transblotted form on a nitrocelluloses, can be a useful tool for the detection of cancer-specific cytochrome c.
